newsitem.title: USA: Giuliani favored in NYC mayor race - poll.
newsitem.headline: Giuliani favored in NYC mayor race - poll.

text.p: Most New Yorkers plan to vote for Mayor Rudolph Giuliani in the city's next election, but they don't like him very much, according to a poll released Tuesday.
The mayor's overall approval rating is at an all-time high of 62 percent, said the poll by Quinnipiac College in Hamden, Connecticut.
Eighty percent said the incumbent Republican has "stong leadership qualities," 84 percent said he "can get things done" and 64 percent found him "honest and trustworthy," the poll showed.
However, 52 percent said Giuliani does not have a "likable personality," 50 percent said he does not work well with others and 55 percent said he is not sympathetic to problems of the poor.
"New Yorkers like the way the mayor does his job, but they don't all like the mayor," said Maurice Carroll, director of the Quinnipiac College Polling Institute.
The poll also showed Giuliani winning more than 50 percent of the vote against any of the potential Democratic mayoral contenders in the November election.

The poll showed Giuliani ahead 55-34 percent over former Mayor David Dinkins, who is considering a return to politics; 54-34 percent ahead of Manhattan Borough President Ruth Messinger; 53-33 percent over Bronx Borough President Fernando Ferrer; 57-23 percent over City Councilman Sal Albanese, and 72-14 percent ahead of the Rev. Al Sharpton.

The poll showed Dinkins handily winning the Democratic primary over other contenders in the race so far. Dinkins, who lost to Giuliani in 1993, has said he will announce whether he will run again on Wednesday.
Voters also approved of the Giuliani administration's handling of crime, which is at its lowest rate in a generation, giving him an 81 percent approval rating.
The poll surveyed 845 city residents who said they were registered voters. It was conducted Feb 3-9 with a margin of error of plus or minus 3.4 percent.
